value.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let 𝔠 denote the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+𝔠[-t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+𝔠[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. For arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs W_1 and W_2, B_avg(W_1×W_2)=B_avg(W_1)+B_avg(W_2), including correlated product-channel input laws and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges a channel's receiver marginals up to bijective output relabeling, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W). Finite products of such receiver-skew channels preserve this equality, and both separately relaxed scalar functionals are exactly additive on every such finite product. For the half-skew BSSC P, the established sharp one-letter BSSC posterior-support inequality and its equality-achieving posterior mixture therefore give B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits for every finite integer n≥1. These conclusions concern only the two separately relaxed scalar UV functionals.

High-precision evaluation of the half-skew BSSC mutual-information identities, support contact point, equality-achieving posterior mixture, receiver-skew channel relations, and normalized exact expression.

Symmetrization of input laws under the receiver-exchanging involution and finite-product closure of that symmetry.
Upper-concave-envelope factorization with forward/reverse chain rules, including cancellation of the cross-coordinate co-information term at equal weighting.
proofs: Analytic product proof deriving subadditivity of both concave-envelope rows from the Csiszár sum identity and product-channel Markov relations, followed by the reverse inequality from product input laws and independent posterior ensembles.
Analytic receiver-skew symmetrization proof establishing equality of the branchwise and averaged scalar functionals and extending the equality and additivity to finite products.

Envelope covariance under a receiver-exchanging involution and concavity at the symmetrized input law prove B_br=B_avg and restriction to invariant laws; coordinatewise relabeling extends the conclusion to finite products.

Exact chain-rule cancellation for correlated product-channel inputs, followed by one-factor envelope bounds and concavity, proves the product upper bound; product priors and product posterior decompositions prove the reverse inequality for B_avg.
Half-skew BSSC specialization combining the fair invariant input law with the dependency-supplied sharp posterior-support inequality and an equality-achieving posterior mixture.

The half-skew BSSC specialization combines the symmetry and product theorem with the established sharp posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving mixture to obtain the exact symbolic value for every finite blocklength.

value.title: Exact product and branchwise additivity for separately relaxed UV scalars

value.currentStateSummary: For finite-alphabet DMBCs, the averaged scalar formed from the two separately relaxed UV sum-rate rows is exactly additive on arbitrary finite products, including correlated product-channel inputs and envelope auxiliaries joint across coordinates. Receiver-skew symmetry makes the corresponding branchwise-minimum scalar equal to the averaged scalar, and finite products of receiver-skew channels inherit equality and exact additivity. For every finite power of the half-skew BSSC, both scalar functionals equal n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits. The new analytic proof and selected computational checks strengthen support for this existing result, but the checks do not establish the global BSSC support inequality, envelope optimization, or product theorem. The theorem does not cover the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or capacity tensorization.
value.localResidualSummary: The two separately relaxed scalar UV functionals cannot gain strength for the BSSC through finite blocking, correlated super-symbol priors, or envelope auxiliaries joint across coordinates. Investigate whether coupled common-auxiliary UV formulations, other weighted scalarizations, the complete UV region, or richer nested auxiliary constraints behave differently and can support a frontier converse; no such extension follows from the established theorem.
value.objective: Determine which UV-derived scalar converse functionals tensorize and whether multiletter coupling can strengthen the BSSC converse.

The code-induced-converse program continues to pursue structure-preserving reduction of finite-block induced laws and channel-specific constraints beyond the coarse entropy/copy relaxation. Separately, exact additivity is established for the averaged separately relaxed UV scalar on arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products and for the branchwise-minimum scalar on finite products of receiver-skew channels. For the half-skew BSSC, both scalars on every finite n-fold product equal n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits, so these particular relaxations do not improve through correlated block inputs or envelope auxiliaries joint across coordinates. This theorem concerns only the two separately relaxed scalar functionals and establishes neither the full UV region nor capacity tensorization or capacity.
